target: Round-17 route "parametric-path": the optimal pair as a function of a uniform stopping probability (labels pp:*), verdict new-barrier

findings.result_name: pp:differ + pp:separation (iii): "the two homotopies differ exponentially"
findings.defect: The result is marked "proved", and the headline asserts "on the same family the bias homotopy of sec:bias makes at most |C| switches, so the two homotopies differ exponentially". The bias half of that separation is MEASURED at D<=5 only. Nothing proved bounds the bias path on BP(D) below thm:lemke-homotopy(c)'s ceiling 2^{|C|}-1 = 4^D-1, which is LARGER than the 2^D-1 of the stopping-probability path; the route's own argument field concedes "(iii) is measured", yet the LaTeX proposition states "has at most |C|=2D" as a fact and pp:separation carries no proof environment. BP(D) is also profile-degenerate in general (F_d and G_d share the readout pair, so f_{F_d,0}(y)=f_{F_d,1}(y) whenever phi_{d-1}=kappa_d under a non-optimal profile), which is exactly the situation in which rem:bias-families records that the count is convention-dependent. What survives as proved is only pp:differ(i): the qualitative statement that the two paths differ, from OS_2 with |C|=1.
findings.evidence: I implemented def:bias / cor:bias-algorithm from the paper's statements (bias.py, bias2.py: harmonic normal form by exact elimination of Vavg, then for each of the 2^{|C|} profiles the affine-in-lambda system (I-Q_pi)y = r_pi - lambda*E_pi, the |C| affine optimality inequalities, and the resulting intervals I_S). Validation: it reproduces rem:bias-families exactly on L_n (cells = n for n=1..7) and RC(k) (cells = k for k=1..7) AND on P_D of thm:fold (cells 0,1,2,3 at D=1..4, which is the paper's "counting distinct breakpoints gives 0,1,2,3 at D<=4"). On BP(D), max over all 4^D base profiles with d=1: cells 1,2,3,6 at D=1,2,3,4 against 1,3,7,15 for the stopping-probability path. That reproduces the route's numbers but is measurement at D<=4 (mine) / D<=5 (theirs), not a bound.

findings.result_name: pp:step: "one step of path-following is the solution of an SSG with |J| controlled vertices"
findings.defect: The proof establishes only that pi^+|_J is AN optimal pair of the derived game D^+; it never shows D^+ has a unique optimal pair on J, so the derived game need not NAME the successor pair. The algorithmic clause in the statement ("Hence one step of path-following is the solution of an SSG with |J| controlled vertices: O(n^3) when |J|=1, 2^{|J|} linear solves in general") is therefore not proved, and is refuted by an explicit instance with |J|=1. GAP, stated exactly: at a breakpoint beta* the pair optimal on (beta*, beta*+eps) is the unique optimal pair of D^+ on J. (The barrier pp:barrier does not depend on this clause, since it uses pp:step only as a per-step cost lower bound.)
findings.evidence: Explicit refutation, exact rational arithmetic (t_double.py): apply pp:one's own gadget construction to P(beta) = (beta-1/2)^2 (A=(1,-4,4), K_0=2, K=4). The result is a 14-vertex ONE-PLAYER stopping SSG (one Max vertex u, thirteen average, trap test: stopping) with val(u_0)-val(u_1) = (1/4)beta^4(beta-1/2)^2 >= 0, verified at beta = 1/4, 2/5, 1/2, 3/5, 3/4, 1. At beta* = 1/2: Opt(1/2) = {0,1} while Opt is the singleton {0} on both sides, so 1/2 IS a breakpoint of the path in the route's own sense (Opt not locally constant), J = {u}; the derived games D^+ and D^- BOTH have two optimal actions {0} and {1}, so the step is ambiguous and one of its two answers is wrong. On the route's own instances the step is unambiguous: I confirmed all 57 breakpoints of BP(1..5) and all 10 of three OS instances, both sides, 67+67 predictions correct and the derived optimum unique in every case; and pp:step(i) exactly (the right derivative of w under pi^+ equals the derived-game value at 11/11 breakpoints of BP(1..3)).

findings.result_name: pp:tent, proof text and why_not_implied: "the naive transplant of thm:fold gives slope 2/beta and dies"
findings.defect: False, and it is the whole of the route's stated design content and of its why_not_implied against thm:fold. Transplanting P_D of thm:fold VERBATIM into G_beta gives fold multiplier beta^2/2 (from X_d -> (t_0,F_{d-1}) followed by the damped controlled step) and constant ratio val(k_{2D-2d+1})/val(k_{2D-2d+3}) = (beta/2)^2 = beta^2/4, hence tent slope exactly (beta^2/2)/(beta^2/4) = 2, beta-INDEPENDENT. The orbit does not "escape [0,1]". What actually fails is the SEED: with u -> (t_0,t_1) one gets phi_0/e_0 = (beta/2)/beta = 1/2 for every beta, whose tent orbit is 1/2, 0, 1, 1, ... , so level 1 is tied identically and no later level ever reverses. Replacing u by the very two-step chain BP(D) already uses for F_0 repairs the verbatim transplant. pp:tent itself is unaffected and reproduces exactly; the defect is the false assertion inside its proof and in why_not_implied, and the consequence that BP(D)'s extra P_d, Q_d, B_d and three-vertex kappa-blocks are not needed.
findings.evidence: t_pd.py, exact. Seed 'u01' (P_D verbatim in G_beta): phi_d/e_d = 1/2, 0, 1, 1, ... at beta=1/3, and 0 changes of Opt across the 2^D interval midpoints with 1 distinct pair, at D=3,4,5 (|V| = 20,26,32). Seed 'chain2' (u replaced by u->(u2,u2), u2->(t1,t1), val beta^2): phi_d/e_d = T^d(beta) with 0 mismatches at 59 rationals for D=3 (177 checks) and D=5 (295 checks), and 7,15,31 breakpoints with 8,16,32 pairwise distinct optimal pairs at D=3,4,5 on |V| = 6D+3 = 21,27,33 vertices. So the same theorem holds on 6D+3 vertices, i.e. 2^{(N-3)/6}-1 breakpoints, against BP(D)'s 2^{(N-2)/10}-1.

findings.defect: pp:basic(c) ("Opt(beta) is a nonempty subcube, namely {pi : pi(v) in argopt_a w_beta(v^{(a)})}") is FALSE at beta = 0, which clause (a) explicitly admits into the theorem's range [0,1). Its proof uses (b) to conclude "pi(v) attains opt_a w_beta(v^{(a)})", a step that divides by beta and is vacuous at beta = 0. Consequently pp:start's "w_0 = 0, so Opt(0) = {0,1}^C and J = C" is false for the J of pp:step (J = {v in C : w(v^0) = w(v^1)}) whenever a controlled vertex has a sink successor: Opt(0) is the full cube by def:pp:def, but J is not C. Fix: restrict (c) to beta in (0,1), and state pp:start's degeneracy in terms of Opt only.
findings.evidence: t_basic.py: the 3-vertex game with one Max vertex v -> (t_0, t_1). w_0 = (0) on V-circle, Opt(0) = both profiles by the definition {pi : T_0 y^pi_0 = y^pi_0}, but argopt_a of the extended w_0 is {1} (w_0(t_1)=1 > w_0(t_0)=0), so (c)'s formula gives the proper subcube {pi(v)=1}, and J = {} while pp:start claims J = C = {v}. (b) itself is fine: 40 random 4-vertex SSGs x all profiles x 9 rationals gave 0 violations of the sign characterisation, with deg N = 4 = n and deg R = 5 = n+1 attained.

findings.result_name: pp:damping (the remark separating the path from the bias homotopy)
findings.defect: The displayed formula "in the harmonic normal form the readouts of G_beta are beta q^{v,a} + beta sum_w p^{v,a}_w y_w" is wrong: damping multiplies each first-passage path by beta^{length}, not by a single beta, so the damped rows are not beta times the undamped ones (and if p,q are read as G_beta's own rows there is no beta at all). The conclusion drawn from it (that M = E(I-Q_1)(I-Q_0)^{-1}E moves with beta, unlike in def:bias) is nevertheless correct.
findings.evidence: Counterexample by direct computation: v in Vmax with action a leading to an average vertex x -> (t_1,t_1). Then val_{G_beta}(v) = beta*val(x) = beta^2, so the readout f_{v,a} = beta^2; the undamped row is q = 1, p = 0, and the route's formula gives beta*1 = beta.

findings.defect: Three statements delivered as proposition/theorem environments carry NO proof environment in the paste-ready LaTeX; their arguments live only in the JSON argument fields. This matters most for pp:robust, which pp:barrier explicitly cites ("by pp:robust this survives both the average-vertices-only damping and the nondegenerate start") and whose part (b) is supported only by the two-sentence sketch "the crossings being transversal ... simple zeros persist for small eps". The sketch is repairable — joint continuity of (beta,eps) |-> w_{beta,c} plus simplicity of the zeros of (beta^2/2)e_{d-1}(T^{d-1}(beta)-1/2) at odd multiples of 2^{-d}, which are interior to the affinity intervals of T^{d-1} — but it is not written, and the non-uniformity of eps_D in D is not addressed.
findings.evidence: Read of the route's latex field: \begin{proposition}\label{pp:start} ... \end{proposition}, \begin{theorem}\label{pp:differ} ... \end{theorem} and \begin{proposition}\label{pp:robust} ... \end{proposition} are each followed directly by the next environment, with no \begin{proof}.

findings.defect: Non-sequitur as written, plus a partial restatement. thm:lemke-homotopy is an LCP homotopy in q, not a parametric linear programme over a fixed polytope, so the one-line LP lemma ("a convex combination of the two inequalities") does not apply to it. The interval property for the bias path is already thm:lemke-homotopy(c) ("the set I_S ... is a closed interval"), unconditionally, and the route does not cite it for this purpose; so the half of (ii) concerning the bias path is a restatement of thm:lemke-homotopy(c) and the half concerning prop:bias-shadow is the only place the LP lemma applies. The conclusion is correct.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex l.8179 thm:lemke-homotopy(c): "for S subseteq C the set I_S of lambda >= 0 whose solution has z_v = 0 off S and (w+lambda d)_v = 0 on S is a closed interval, on which z_S(lambda) = -(M_SS)^{-1}(q_S+lambda d_S) is affine" — proved with no nondegeneracy hypothesis (that hypothesis is used only for the step-function / distinctness clause).

findings.result_name: pp:differ(i): "exactly one [switch], at lambda = d_v/32, from base profile 1"
findings.defect: The covering vector is on the wrong side. By thm:lemke-homotopy(b), lambda_0 = max_v max(0, -q_v/d_v) = (1/32)/d_v on OS_2 from base 1, not d_v/32; the two agree only at d_v = 1.
findings.evidence: My bias implementation on OS_2 with d = 1 (t_misc.py): base (0,) gives lambda_0 = 0 with 0 cells (no switch); base (1,) gives lambda_0 = 1/32 with exactly 1 cell (one switch). The readouts at beta = 1 are f_{v,0} = 11/32 and f_{v,1} = 10/32 = 5/16, as claimed.

findings.result_name: pp:separation, validation of the route's bias implementation
findings.defect: The claim that the implementation "reproduces rem:bias-families exactly" is only partly true: on P_D of thm:fold the route reports 0,2,3,4,7,8 distinct breakpoints at D=1..6, while rem:bias-families records 0,1,2,3 at D<=4 and an independent implementation validated on L_n, RC(k) AND P_D gives 0,1,2,3. The route labels the disagreement "a fourth convention-dependent reading" without exhibiting the convention. Its BP(D) numbers under the switch-all-vanishing reading do agree with mine, so the substantive conclusion at D<=4 is unaffected.
findings.evidence: t_bias_val.py / t_misc.py: my cell count is n on L_n (n=1..7), k on RC(k) (k=1..7) and 0,1,2,3 on P_D (D=1..4) — three-for-three with rem:bias-families; and it reproduces thm:fold's value identity val(F_D) = 3*2^{-D-2} at D=2..6 (3/16, 3/32, 3/64, 3/128, 3/256), which the route also reports.

findings.defect: G_D is not reachable from F_D: the only in-edges of G_d come from Q_{d+1}, which does not exist at d = D. So the subgame reachable from the natural root has 10D+1 vertices, D Max and D-1 Min. Nothing breaks (F_D still reverses at the same 2^{D-1} points, and the breakpoint set is unchanged), but "D Max and D Min vertices" describes the presented game rather than the game as posed from a root.
findings.evidence: Direct reading of the successor lists: F_d and G_d both point to (X_d, Y_d); the only vertex pointing at G_d is Q_{d+1} -> (G_d, G_d).

findings.result_name: pp:barrier, the class of the witness families
findings.defect: BP(D), BP'(D), BP^a(D) and OS(R) are all acyclic, hence lie in thm:avg-acyclic (and thm:kacyclic) and are solved in linear time by backward induction. The barrier is therefore a mechanism barrier on a family the paper already solves — the same situation as thm:fold's P_D. The route does not claim otherwise, but does not say so either, and pp:barrier's "no continuation method ... is polynomial" would read better with the qualification.
findings.evidence: topo_order() succeeds on every instance built (BP(1..9), BP'(1..6), BP^a(1..8), OS(k) for k=1..8), and the trap test of lem:trapchar returns the empty trap in every case.

findings.defect: The heuristic offered for why the fold has no one-player form ("every one-player value is a nonnegative combination of the sink payoffs and max alone is monotone; and pp:monotone shows that no single value beta |-> w_beta(v) can fold") does not obstruct one-player folding, since the object that must fold is a DIFFERENCE of values and pp:one already exhibits one-player differences with k sign changes. The missing statement is correctly flagged as a GAP; only the accompanying reason is weak.
findings.evidence: pp:one, verified: OS(R) is one-player and val(u_0) - val(u_1) = 2^{K_0-K} beta^K prod_i(beta - r_i) changes sign k times, with action strings 10, 010, 1010, 01010, 101010, 0101010, 10101010, 010101010 at k=1..8.

verdict: The route's central positive claims reproduce EXACTLY, from the statements, in exact rational arithmetic, with an independent core. pp:tent: BP(D) built from the statement is stopping (trap test), has N=10D+2 with D Max and D Min, satisfies kappa_d=(beta/2)(beta^3/4)^{d-1} and phi_d=T^d(beta)e_d with 0 mismatches out of 597,995,1393,1791,2189,2587,2985,3383 checks at 199 rationals j/200 for D=1..8, agrees with brute force over all 4^D profiles at 7 rationals for D<=4 (and Opt is there exactly the argopt subcube), and has exactly 2^D-1 breakpoints at {k/2^D} with 2^D pairwise distinct optimal pairs, |J|=2 at every breakpoint and no extra breakpoint at 6 interior rationals of non-dyadic denominator per interval, for D=1..9; F_D reverses 2^{D-1} times, val(F_D)(beta=1)=2^{-D}, last breakpoint 1-2^{-D}. pp:robust reproduces: BP^a(D) on 9D+3 = 12,...,75 vertices with average-only damping (0 mismatches at 99 rationals, 2^D-1 breakpoints, D<=8) and the c-variant with c_v=2^{-(14D+30)}(v+1) (no tie at beta=0; exactly 1,3,7,16,33,64,129 changes over 2^{D+2} samples at D=1..7, matching the route's numbers digit for digit). BP'(D) reproduces on 12D+2 vertices with no two controlled vertices sharing a successor pair. pp:one reproduces: |V| = 8,17,32,61,94,129,169,250 and K = 2,4,7,11,15,18,21,28 for k=1..8, the identity val(u_0)-val(u_1)=2^{K_0-K}beta^K P(beta) with 0 mismatches at 59 rationals, alternating actions and ties exactly at R; OS_2 has 19 vertices, A=(3,-10,8), K=5, difference (1/4)beta^5(beta-1/2)(beta-3/4), path 0,1,0. pp:step's mathematics is correct: the first-order identity u^+ = r + beta* P u^+ is exactly the differentiated fixed-point equation (verified exactly at 11/11 breakpoints of BP(1..3)) and the derived-game prediction was right at all 67 right-hand and 67 left-hand cases. pp:basic(b) verified on 40 random games with the degree bounds attained. The damping restatement (G_beta at beta=1-2^{-m} IS def:damping's G_m) verified against the literal edge-chain construction on 45 stopping instances, 0 mismatches. So the barrier itself -- 2^{Omega(N)} breakpoints on the stopping-probability path, surviving both average-only damping and a nondegenerate start -- STANDS. Three major defects survive, none of them fatal to that barrier. (1) The second half of the headline, the EXPONENTIAL separation from the bias homotopy, is measured at D<=5 only; nothing proved bounds the bias path on BP(D) below 4^D-1, and the result is nevertheless marked "proved". (2) pp:step's algorithmic clause ("one step of path-following is the solution of an SSG with |J| controlled vertices") is refuted by an explicit 14-vertex one-player stopping SSG on which beta*=1/2 is a breakpoint, |J|=1, and both actions are optimal in the derived game; the proved content is only that the successor pair is AN optimal pair of it. (3) The stated reason why thm:fold's P_D cannot be transplanted -- "the direct transplant gives slope 2/beta and dies" -- is false: the verbatim transplant has slope exactly 2, and what kills it is the constant seed phi_0/e_0 = 1/2; giving it BP(D)'s own two-step seed makes the verbatim P_D transplant work, with 2^D-1 breakpoints on 6D+3 vertices instead of 10D+2, which I built and verified. Minor defects: pp:basic(c) and pp:start's "J = C" are false at beta=0 (3-vertex witness); pp:damping's readout formula for G_beta is wrong (the damping is beta^{path length}, not beta); pp:start, pp:differ and pp:robust are delivered with no proof environment; pp:differ(ii)'s inference to thm:lemke-homotopy is a non-sequitur and its bias-path half restates thm:lemke-homotopy(c); "lambda = d_v/32" should be (1/32)/d_v; and the route's bias implementation over-counts P_D by one against both the paper and an independent implementation. I found no instance of the project's standing traps: no dict-literal row collapse (all rows accumulated), no fresh-vertex/sink collision (sentinels), no greedy policy iteration in a possibly non-stopping game (every value computed by profile enumeration or acyclic backward induction), t0 correctly excluded from the trap along with t1, no unreachable vertex used to separate a family (my pruned OS(R) sizes match the route's exactly), no vacuous stall or pair-test-for-decision-rule issue (the route makes no decision-rule claim), no fifth imported theorem, and no step assuming a target-equivalent oracle beyond the acknowledged 2^{|J|} cost of pp:step.
